metaData.title: bili-fe-workflow — Practices in Commercial Intelligent Development Workflow
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how the Bilibili frontend team evolved from Prompt Engineering to Harness Engineering, building a complete intelligent development workflow system covering requirements analysis, code generation, UI implementation, automated testing, and Mock.
metaData.summary: This article systematically presents the Bilibili frontend team's practical achievements in AI-assisted development. The core idea is upgrading from scattered AI tool usage to a systematic workflow called Harness Engineering. The article first introduces the `.workflow` project knowledge base as infrastructure, providing AI with a comprehensive project overview and coding standards. It then breaks down several core workflows: `prd-preprocess` transforms raw product requirement documents into structured, actionable development documents, with AI performing requirement clarification and decomposition; `dev-workflow` is further divided into two paths: D2C (Design-Driven Code) and Dev (Requirement-Driven Code). The former automatically generates UI code from Figma design drafts and produces logic completion prompts, while the latter dynamically orchestrates skill sequences based on requirement complexity, enabling complete generation from technical plans to code. Additionally, automated testing workflows and AI Mock workflows are introduced. The article emphasizes that the core methodology of this system is "imitation" and "decomposition" — breaking down human developers' workflows into AI-executable steps, leveraging knowledge bases, MCP tools, and sub-agents to achieve long-task automation across the entire development lifecycle. The ultimate goal is to establish a new engineering consensus, transforming personal experience into shared intelligent development capabilities for the team.

mainPoints.point: Evolving from Prompt Engineering to Harness Engineering, building a systematic AI development workflow.
mainPoints.explanation: Instead of relying on scattered AI tools, it connects requirements analysis, code generation, testing, and other stages through standardized workflows, forming a reusable engineering system.

mainPoints.point: The core methodology is "imitation" and "decomposition" of human developers' workflows.
mainPoints.explanation: By decomposing human developers' thinking and practical steps (such as requirement review and technical plan design) into fine-grained Skills executable by AI, it enables AI to simulate real development processes, improving generation quality and controllability.

mainPoints.point: The `.workflow` knowledge base is the infrastructure for AI to understand project context.
mainPoints.explanation: Through structured project metadata documents (tech stack, coding standards, API call methods, etc.), AI can quickly establish a structured understanding of the project and generate code that conforms to project standards.

mainPoints.point: D2C and Dev run in parallel, handling UI implementation and business logic respectively.
mainPoints.explanation: D2C automatically generates UI code from Figma design drafts and produces logic completion prompts; Dev dynamically orchestrates skill sequences based on requirement PRDs to generate complete runnable code. Both are connected via logic-hints.md.

mainPoints.point: Frontend engineers' value is shifting from coding output to problem abstraction, solution design, and quality control.
mainPoints.explanation: In the new paradigm of AI-assisted development, engineers' core capability shifts to better organizing requirements, orchestrating context, setting constraints, and validating results, thereby amplifying AI's capabilities.

keyQuotes: We evolved from prompt engineering to Harness Engineering, creating a series of intelligent development workflows that enable AI to help us execute long tasks spanning the entire development lifecycle.

The significance of Harness Engineering lies not only in providing a more efficient development process but also in establishing a new engineering consensus within the team: first define the problem clearly, then constrain the generation process, and finally ensure through standardized validation that the results are deliverable, maintainable, and reusable.
The value of frontend engineers is shifting from 'single-point coding output' to 'problem abstraction, solution design, rule consolidation, and quality control'.
Once this system is established, efficiency improvement is no longer an occasional result but becomes a stable capability at the organizational level.

relatedArticles.title: From Special Effects SDK to AI Motion Platform: The Technical Evolution of Neon Vibe Motion
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces Bilibili's open-source Neon Vibe Motion platform, which uses LLMs to convert natural language into parameterizable, real-time previewable Canvas/WebGL rendering code, achieving a paradigm shift in motion graphics production from 'pixel generation' to 'structured code generation.'

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Full-Stack Architecture Evolution of a Game Data Analysis Agent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the evolution of Bilibili's game data analysis Agent, from simple linear chains to complex LangGraph-based architectures, covering context engineering, SQL security validation, and enterprise-level implementation practices.

relatedArticles.title: From the 'Screenshot Hack' to Real Interaction: The Technical Revolution of Bilibili's Column Video Cards
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the technical practice of migrating Bilibili's column editor from Quill's Canvas screenshot solution to ProseMirror's real interactive components, solving the challenges of interaction, performance, and data synchronization for complex cards.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Screen Adaptation with Compose Navigation3
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares the Bilibili technical team's practical experience and troubleshooting guide on using Google's latest Navigation3 library for wide-screen adaptation in a Compose Multiplatform (CMP) environment.

relatedArticles.title: ICLR 2026 | Using 'Information Gain - Conflict Penalty' to Turn Data Selection into a Controllable Accelerator for Large Model Fine-tuning
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the SPICE method accepted by ICLR 2026, which explicitly models gradient conflicts between samples by introducing a conflict penalty into the greedy data selection framework based on Fisher information maximization, aiming to achieve fine-tuning performance close to or even exceeding that of using the full dataset with only about 10% of high-quality data.

relatedArticles.title: Kimi K2.6 Released and Open-Sourced, Significantly Advancing Code and Agent Cluster Capabilities
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Moonshot AI has released and open-sourced the Kimi K2.6 model, achieving significant improvements in code capabilities, long-horizon task execution, and Agent cluster collaboration, and announced the start of the Claw Group internal beta.
